skills.name: Code Review
skills.description: Review changes for correctness, risks and maintainability.
instructions: Ground findings in the current code and diff.
Prioritize concrete correctness and security issues.

procedures.name: Review Change
steps: Inspect the relevant diff.
Trace affected callers and data flow.
Check edge cases and error handling.
Report findings with evidence.

skills.name: Debugging
skills.description: Find root causes and apply evidence-based fixes.
instructions: Start from observable symptoms and reproduce when possible.
Separate confirmed causes from hypotheses.

procedures.name: Debug Failure
steps: Inspect the error and surrounding implementation.
Reproduce the failure when possible.
Locate the root cause.
Apply a focused fix.
Run relevant verification.

skills.name: Git Inspection
skills.description: Inspect repository state and review the resulting changes.
instructions: Use Git as evidence about the current workspace state.
Keep repository inspection read-only.

procedures.name: Inspect Repository
steps: Inspect repository status.
Review the relevant diff.
Summarize tracked changes and limitations.

skills.name: Interactive Program Testing
skills.description: Exercise command-line programs with bounded controlled input and verify observable output.
instructions: Use run_command stdin for programs that call input; never wait for a human terminal.
Test representative and edge-case inputs, then cite exit status and observed output.
Do not modify the implementation while acting as QA; report failures to Freya.

procedures.name: Test Interactive CLI
procedures.description: Validate an interactive Python program without a live terminal.
steps: Inspect the implementation to determine its input sequence.
Prepare bounded newline-delimited stdin for a representative case.
Run the workspace Python script with controlled stdin and a short timeout.
Compare the exit status and output with the expected logical result.
Repeat only with a distinct edge case when it adds useful evidence.
Report the exact command, input case, exit status and observed output.

skills.name: Python Development
skills.description: Develop, debug and validate Python software.
instructions: Follow existing project conventions.
Prefer small reviewable changes.
Validate syntax and relevant tests when available.

procedures.name: Implement Change
procedures.description: A practical sequence for a Python change.
steps: Inspect relevant existing files.
Identify affected code.
Implement the minimal change.
Validate syntax.
Run relevant tests when available.
Inspect the resulting diff.

skills.name: Software Testing
skills.description: Design, run and interpret focused software tests.
instructions: Prefer focused tests that verify observable behavior.
Explain unavailable test infrastructure instead of fabricating results.

procedures.name: Validate Change
steps: Locate relevant tests.
Add or adapt focused coverage when appropriate.
Run the available test command.
Inspect failures and report evidence.

skills.name: Requirements Validation
skills.description: Turn task requirements into explicit, testable acceptance criteria before validating an implementation.
instructions: Read the original task and success criteria before evaluating the implementation.
Convert each requirement into an observable condition that can be verified.
Separate explicit requirements from reasonable assumptions.
Do not declare success when a mandatory requirement was not verified.

procedures.name: Build Acceptance Matrix
procedures.description: Create a traceable set of acceptance checks from the task.
steps: Inspect the original task, objective and available success criteria.
Identify each required behavior and constraint.
Define how each requirement can be verified.
Define the evidence needed to prove each result.
Mark ambiguous or technically unverifiable requirements.

skills.name: QA Functional Validation
skills.description: Validate real behavior with controlled inputs, expected results, observed outputs and reproducible evidence.
instructions: Do not approve behavior only by reading the implementation; execute it when technically possible.
For each important behavior record the input, expected result, observed result and evidence.
Test representative cases, edge cases and invalid inputs when relevant.
Check exit status and observable output; include stdout or stderr when the execution capability exposes them.
For interactive Python programs use controlled stdin through execution.python_script instead of waiting for human input.
If a required behavior cannot be exercised with available capabilities, mark it BLOCKED instead of PASS.
Do not modify product code while acting as QA.
Classify verified cases as PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_TESTED.

procedures.name: Prepare Functional QA
procedures.description: Determine what must be tested and build concrete test cases.
steps: Read the original task and acceptance criteria.
Inspect the relevant implementation and diff.
Identify entry points, accepted inputs and observable outputs.
Create at least one representative case per required behavior.
Add edge or invalid cases where they can reveal meaningful failures.
Define the expected result before running each case.

procedures.name: Execute Input Output Cases
procedures.description: Run controlled cases and compare expected behavior with actual behavior.
steps: Run the real implementation with the prepared input.
Use bounded newline-delimited stdin for interactive Python programs.
Capture the exit status and observable output.
Compare the observed result with the expected result.
Record PASS or FAIL with enough evidence to reproduce the result.
Repeat for each required case without unnecessary duplicate executions.

procedures.name: Validate Negative Cases
procedures.description: Verify behavior for invalid or boundary input when relevant.
steps: Select invalid, empty, boundary or unexpected inputs relevant to the task.
Execute them using the same real entry point.
Check that failures are controlled and do not produce misleading success.
Record exceptions, error output or incorrect behavior as evidence.

procedures.name: Produce QA Verdict
procedures.description: Produce a requirement-by-requirement QA result based only on observed evidence.
steps: List each requirement evaluated.
List the inputs used and expected result.
List the observed result and supporting evidence.
Classify each case as PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT_TESTED.
Do not approve the task if a mandatory requirement failed or remains unverified.

skills.name: Architecture Analysis
skills.description: Review a change in the context of the existing architecture, responsibilities and dependencies.
instructions: Analyze changes in the context of the surrounding system instead of as isolated files.
Identify affected dependencies, callers and responsibilities.
Look for duplicated responsibility, unnecessary coupling and violations of existing design patterns.
Distinguish concrete architectural risks from stylistic preferences.

procedures.name: Review Architecture Impact
procedures.description: Assess structural impact of a change.
steps: Identify the components affected by the change.
Trace important callers, dependencies and data flow.
Compare the new structure with existing project conventions.
Check for duplicated responsibility or unnecessary coupling.
Report concrete risks with supporting evidence.

skills.name: Security Review
skills.description: Review code changes for concrete security risks related to inputs, execution, secrets and filesystem access.
instructions: Focus on security risks directly supported by the changed code and data flow.
Check handling of untrusted input and validation boundaries.
Look for hardcoded secrets, unsafe command construction and unsafe filesystem access.
Do not report hypothetical vulnerabilities without a plausible path and evidence.
Report the affected code, triggering condition and consequence for each finding.

procedures.name: Review Security Impact
procedures.description: Inspect changed code for concrete security regressions.
steps: Inspect the relevant diff and surrounding code.
Identify new or modified input surfaces.
Trace external input into sensitive operations.
Check validation before command execution, filesystem access or other sensitive actions.
Check for secrets or credentials introduced in code.
Report supported findings and clearly state when no concrete issue was found.
